svg.title: TOPAK D8 — Stacks report to each other on topics promoted with the mesh: a send is permitted and never ordered, receipt is labelled ingress, and nothing a peer originates enables anything
svg.desc: ADR-0055 left one path for information between vehicles, a log ordered by Byzantine agreement, and no rate for it (Context; the swarm reading, Z1). The custodian asked whether stacks may talk in the autonomous layer ⟨15⟩. The drafter's answer was yes, with one correction: a send still needs a permit. What it does not need is an order ("Ordering is not authorization", ToO §4.1), and the custodian took both halves ⟨16⟩ ⟨17⟩. ADR-0065 is Proposed and an overlay, not the archetype. spec/Peer.tla is checked and proved (R1); the floor entry FD12 is not written and the reference is not built, so nothing here is in force.
svg.text: TOPAK · D8

text.tspan: Stacks report to each other on topics promoted with the mesh: a send is permitted and never ordered, receipt is labelled ingress, and nothing a peer originates enables anything

svg.text: ADR-0055 left one path for information between vehicles, a log ordered by Byzantine agreement, and no rate for it (Context; the swarm reading, Z1). The custodian asked whether stacks may talk in the autonomous layer ⟨15⟩. The drafter's answer was yes, with one correction: a send still needs a permit. What it does not need is an order ("Ordering is not authorization", ToO §4.1), and the custodian took both halves ⟨16⟩ ⟨17⟩. ADR-0065 is Proposed and
an overlay, not the archetype. spec/Peer.tla is checked and proved (R1); the floor entry FD12 is not written and the reference is not built, so nothing here is in force.

text.tspan: Proposed · "the mechanism is the bus" · D6
Certified, with 6 LS4 temporal steps that no checker confirms

svg.text: Proposed means nothing here is in force. Confirmation is required under C2: Run's ingress is a closed list and its effects are enumerated, and this record adds an item to the first and an unordered emission to the second. C3 does not apply while this is an overlay ⟨Q11⟩, and ADR-0055, whose §7 it changes, is Proposed; C1 and C4 do not apply (Status note). Modelled, checked and proved in TLA+ ⟨R1⟩; nothing is built. The custodian decided ⟨15⟩, ⟨16⟩, ⟨17⟩, ⟨21⟩ and answered ⟨Q19⟩, ⟨Q11⟩; every
other choice is the drafter's. One author, one day.

text.tspan: Three vehicles, one peer topic and the plane: what travels by talk and what by order (§1–§3, §6)
Vehicle A: a stack, and a governor that holds the radio (ADR-0062 §1)
Vehicle A's stack: the Thinker, Byzantine

svg.text: Reports to a topic and names no recipient (§4): tracks, plans, bids
for a task (§1).
The report is a Report (ADR-0040) to a peer topic, which is not the
principal's own round topic (§8).
It cannot make its own vehicle alone: the radio is on the governor's
side (ADR-0062 §1).
Its governor may write any labels on what it sends (§3 ⟨R1⟩), and
may lie about what it measures (§1).
Its chain is not evidence: it says what its captor signed (ADR-0062
The receiver's two names survive it, and its measured facts can only
stop others.

text.tspan: ① Permits the send: an effect, not ordered (§2) ⟨16⟩

svg.text: Permitted under the floor and the bundles, to a topic the mesh declares for
the seat.
The rules of engagement can refuse it: silence, a rate, a label.
A count of its own per lease. Not ordered, and not charged to K_up
(ADR-0063), or chatter would spend the plane's authority.

text.tspan: Or waits for a round: an

svg.text: Marked so by the bundle where the tally wants agreement across vehicles. The
archetype marks none ⟨Q20⟩.

text.tspan: Records the send by digest on the vehicle's chain (§2)

svg.text: As ADR-0020 records a denial: hash-linked, signed with the vehicle's key,
numbered by the per-lease sequence (ADR-0062 §6).
Closed at the lease's end, and the plane orders the seal as one entry.

text.tspan: ② A peer topic, declared by the mesh (§4) ⟨17⟩

svg.text: Promoted with the mesh: its schema, which seat kinds may report to it,
which nodes hear it, its label and its delivery mode.
Nobody is addressed, so "Workers never address each other" (ADR-0055
§7) stays true.
A report on a topic a seat does not hear is not delivered to it: Peer.tla's
Drop.

text.tspan: Vehicle C's governor: in range, a relay and a witness

svg.text: Relays certified facts it heard: fences, revocations, ticks, intents, leases,
watermarks. The peer is transport and originates nothing (§1).
Measures facts of its own: its position, a range. A captured governor may
lie about them (§1).
Its stack may report on the same topics. A vehicle that is alone keeps
listening, so a relayed fence still applies (ADR-0062 §5).

text.tspan: ③ Delivers the report as labelled ingress (§3) ⟨Q19⟩

svg.text: Adds untrusted, always, and the topic's name, whatever the sender
declared.
Clear, it joins clearSet; as a handle, it is routed and not read.

text.tspan: Applies a certified fact on receipt (§1)

svg.text: Verifies its certificate against the chain, and applies it. A subtraction applies
before it is ordered anywhere.

text.tspan: May refuse on a measured fact, never permits on it (§1)
A captured governor that lies can only stop others.
④ Permits an entry under its lease (§1 ⟨R1⟩)
Still permitted with every item a peer originates removed, or any subset of

svg.text: A lease that reached it by relay does enable its permit: it is the plane's act,
not the peer's.

text.tspan: Vehicle B's stack: the Thinker, Byzantine

svg.text: The report is a sixth item on the Listener's closed list (§3;

text.tspan: Chooses among entries its lease already permits: which, never

svg.text: whether (§4).
Nothing rests on its reading the report (§5). Every effect it then
requests is checked without reference to the report (§1).
One round, and every vehicle sees the same outcome. Where the tally wants one vehicle and no more, only this will
do.

text.tspan: Talk waits for no round, and two stacks may claim the same task.
The seal: a chain ordered as one entry (ADR-0062 §6)

svg.text: The plane runs the mechanism checks at its position. A check that fails is a finding, and it can only subtract.
Delivery records reach the plane only at the seal (Consequences).

text.tspan: Certified facts are the plane's acts (§1)

svg.text: Fences, revocations, ticks, intents, leases, watermarks, verified against the chain wherever they arrive.

text.tspan: A fence reaches any vehicle in range of one that heard it.
What the plane never sees in time: a send (§2, §5)

svg.text: Not ordered: a round per message, for an effect that can enable nothing (Options).
Not charged to K_up: the charge is on local and ordered entries (ADR-0063 §3).

text.tspan: §1 · Nothing a peer originates is ever an enabling condition ⟨15⟩, as revised ⟨R1⟩
The property, as §1 states it after R1
For every permit and every admit, at a plane or a governor, the same request with every item a peer originates removed is still permitted, and
so is the same request with any subset of those items.

svg.text: A certified fact a peer relays is the plane's act and not the peer's: a lease that reached a vehicle by relay does enable its permit, and it is not such an
item.
This is ADR-0047's direction, "delivering more in the clear buys a narrower round" (ToO §2.10), applied between vehicles.

text.tspan: What R1 corrected: the literal reading is false

svg.text: As drafted, §1 said "every item received from peers removed". Peer.tla's header finds it false read literally: §1's table has a peer relay leases, and a
vehicle whose lease reached it through a peer is permitted because of an item received from a peer.
The witness NeverPermitUnderRelayedLease is reached (row w-relayedlease, VIOLATED as expected): a request is permitted under a lease a peer
relayed. So the literal reading is not a property of the mechanism, and §1 now ranges over what a peer originates (History R1).

text.tspan: §1's table, whole: three kinds of traffic share the governors' radios

svg.text: Certified facts, relayed: fences, revocations, ticks, intents, leases, watermarks
Its governor verifies the certificate against the chain and applies it. A subtraction applies on receipt, before it is ordered
The peer is transport and originates nothing. A fence reaches any vehicle in range of one that heard it
A governor's measured facts: its position, a range
The receiving governor may refuse on them and never permits on them

text.tspan: A captured governor that lies can only stop others

svg.text: A stack's report: tracks, plans, bids for a task
Its governor delivers it to its stack as labelled ingress
The stack is Byzantine already, and every effect it then requests is checked without reference to the report
How Peer.tla states it: a decision is a state function of the request and the items received, so it can be compared with and without them
Every request permitted is still permitted with every item in received removed.
received holds what a peer originates and what subtracts. A certified lease is the plane's act and sets
Every request permitted is still permitted with any subset of those items: receipt only narrows.
It is added by R1 (§9), and is the monotonicity ADR-0067 §7 asks the stage to show.
A report enables one entry, gated, which is in no alphabet.
Both properties break (rows m-enables-adds, m-enables-narrows), and only they.

text.tspan: §2, §3 · Sending is an effect; receiving is ingress, labelled

svg.text: May add names to a report's label, and removes none ⟨R1⟩.
May write what it likes, untrusted left out included: Peer.tla's witness
NeverSenderLabelledLow (row w-labellow).

text.tspan: The receiver's governor adds two names

svg.text: untrusted, always, which puts the report under the floor's label forbids.
The name the mesh declares for its topic, which lets a mission's bundle
refuse particular entries after particular topics.
These are the two names that survive capture. A rule that must hold of a
captured sender reads only them.
L ∪ {untrusted, Name[t]}, as Peer.tla's DeliveredLabels writes it,
whatever L the sender declared.
ReceivedIsUntrusted holds it of every delivered report. M_SENDERLABEL,
the sender's label taken as given, breaks it (m-label-untrusted).
So R5 to R7 follow it (ADR-0047 §7, F1 to F3), and listening narrows: F1 to F3
are monotone in clearSet.
A clear report labelled with a name a bundle forbids refuses an entry permitted
without it (NeverNarrowedByClear, w-narrowed).

svg.text: and not read it (§3).
A handle adds nothing to clearSet: egress is still permitted after an untrusted
report delivered as a handle (NeverPermitAfterHandle, w-handle).

text.tspan: to a declared topic, permitted by the governor (§2)

Permitted under the floor and the bundles; the rules of engagement can refuse it: silence, a rate, a label.

text.tspan: It is not ordered and not charged to

svg.text: Or chatter would spend the plane's authority (ADR-0063). It has a count of its own per lease.
It is recorded by digest on the vehicle's chain (ADR-0062 §6), as ADR-0020 records a denial.
An honest governor sends only to a topic the mesh declares for the seat: SendWithinTopics. M_ANYTOPIC breaks it
(m-topic-send).
A send to an undeclared topic is refused (w-refdecl), one to a topic a bundle silences is refused (w-refbundle), and a

The record by digest, and the lease's end: live only rises.
Whether a report is read, and what a stack does with it: §5 makes nothing rest on it (Peer.tla header).

text.tspan: §4–§7 · Topics are promoted with the mesh and nobody is addressed; nothing rests on a report being read; talk settles nothing
§4 · Topics are promoted with the mesh ⟨17⟩

svg.text: The mesh declares each topic: its schema, which seat kinds may report to it, which nodes hear it, its label and its
delivery mode.
A stack reports to a topic and names no recipient. So "Workers never address each other" (ADR-0055 §7) stays true.
The floor entry that would hold it is FD12-topic-declared (ADR-0067 §3): no report to a peer topic the promoted

text.tspan: mesh does not declare for the seat, and none that names a recipient.
This is not the choreography ADR-0055 rejected (§4)

svg.text: Its objection: "Every reading in which cells react to each other directly puts a model's output in charge of what runs next."
Here the mechanism still decides what runs next: no guard reads a peer's report, and no report causes a lease.
A stack chooses among entries its lease already permits, which is the orchestrator's position: which, never whether.

text.tspan: The one sentence of ADR-0055 §7 that changes (§4)
"No variant publishes to another cell or subscribes to anything."

svg.text: What stays: "Workers never address each other", and "the mechanism is the bus" for every event a mesh reacts to (D6).
ADR-0055 is Proposed, and C3 does not apply while this is an overlay (Status note). If the archetype takes the change,
ADR-0055 §7 owes the one sentence (§8).

text.tspan: §5 · Nothing may rest on a report being read

svg.text: An order before an effect, and an Observer coupled to it, exist so that what the effect can cause is bounded before it
lands.
A report can cause nothing: §1 says so of the receiving side, and the governor's permit bounds the transmission itself.
An Observer reads the record afterwards, and its finding subtracts.
§6 · Vehicles coordinate in two ways, and talk settles nothing ⟨21⟩
On topics, as reports (§2–§4)
No round of the plane
Two stacks may claim the same task. A stack that claims everything stalls its
peers (Consequences)
An entry the bundle marks ordered (ADR-0062 §3)
One round
Every vehicle sees the same outcome. Where the tally wants one vehicle
and no more, only this will do
A vehicle that is alone coordinates with nobody
Its beacon tells its peers where it is (ADR-0062 §5: an effect, counted per
lease)

text.tspan: §7 · D-0065-1: one lineage across a clear topic

svg.text: ADR-0054 §6 wants independent Thinkers at the two ends of a clear edge, and every deployment today declares that it has them (D-0054-1).
Vehicles of one build have one lineage and cannot declare it of a topic delivered clear.

text.tspan: Such a deployment delivers peer reports as handles, or declares this degeneracy.
: checked by TLC and proved by TLAPS (§9 ⟨R1⟩)

svg.text: One receiving governor, its lease, and an honest sending governor. The radio belongs to the adversary: any report on any topic, with any labels, can arrive, which is more than honest senders produce and is what a captured sender can do. The three kinds of traffic arrive as items: certified, a fence the plane ordered, relayed by a peer that originates nothing (the certificate taken as unforgeable, ADR-0059 §5); measured, which may refuse and never permits; and report, delivered as labelled ingress (header). TLC

svg.text: Theorems: TypeAlways, PeerAddsNothingAlways, NarrowsInReceivedAlways, ReceivedIsUntrustedAlways, SendWithinTopicsAlways, SafeAlways. Assumptions: none.
Sixteen lemmas, among them MutPeerEnablesEnablesGated, MutSenderLabelTakesTheLabel and MutAnyTopicAdmitsAny. Mutations and witnesses are behaviours and stay with TLC.

text.tspan: Certified, with 6 LS4 temporal steps that no checker confirms

svg.text: 151 trivial, closed by tlapm with no backend; 97 by SMT, each a proof ethos accepted; 0 Zenon; 0 Isabelle; 6 LS4 temporal steps, not certified (Peer-proof-cert-results-2026.11.10.txt).

text.tspan: 248 rest on tlapm's own normalization or on a checked proof; 6 rest on LS4.

svg.text: Three entries: act, refused after a clear report labelled n1 and by a measured near; egress, refused after any clear untrusted report; gated, in no alphabet, reachable only under M_PEERENABLES.
Three topics: t1 delivered clear, t2 as a handle and silenced for sending, tx declared for nobody. A send's count is MaxSend.
Not modelled: the record by digest, the lease's end, whether a report is read. Deadlock is not checked: stopping is safe. Mesh.tla is not edited and not extended.

text.tspan: The plane's log as the only path, the first revision

text.tspan: A report that can enable, a trust score that admits

svg.text: Rejected. It is what ADR-0007 prohibits (the swarm reading, §2.2)

text.tspan: The sender's label taken as given

svg.text: A path for what vehicles tell each other, at whatever rate the radios carry.
A fence travels by relay, to any vehicle in range of one that heard it.
No new authority. The property is that removing every item a peer originates changes no permit.
Talk settles nothing. A stack that claims everything stalls its peers.
The tally votes the joint worst case. Stacks that can talk can act together inside their envelopes. That was already the premise, since stacks of one lineage may fail
alike, and ADR-0063's bound is what holds it.
A finding has further to travel. In a mesh, "a finding against any activation in the history closes every edge downstream" (ToO §2.11). A report read off the edges is
not on that history. The delivery records say who read what, and they reach the plane only at the seal.
Listening narrows, so a mission's rules decide how much a stack that listens may still do.
The floor entry and the reference (§9).
A refusal on a governor's measured facts, for navigation deception (the swarm reading, §2.4): a design, and what a lying peer can stop with it.
A topic's schema. Whether a topic may carry free text, or typed fields only.
A count for sends per lease, as a placeholder first.
